chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), that Mujahid, the freedman of Abdullah ibn al-Abbas, entered upon him and said:

"O Commander of the Faithful, what do you say about the speech/teaching of the People of Qadr?" And with him was a group of people. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said, "Is one of them with you, or is one of them in the house?" He said, "What will you do with them, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said, "I will ask them to repent (istatibu-hum). If they repent, [well and good], and if not, I will strike their necks."

key_terms.أَسْتَتِيبُهُمْ: I will ask them to repent / I will seek their repentance
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْقَدَرِ: People of Qadr (a theological group emphasizing divine decree)
key_terms.ضَرَبْتُ أَعْنَاقَهُمْ: I will strike their necks (idiom for execution/beheading)

ai.seo_question: What is Imam Ali's ruling on the People of Qadr if they do not repent?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the method of *istitab* (granting time for repentance) before executing the Ahl al-Qadr, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle of distinguishing between mere doctrinal error and persistent heresy warranting capital punishment. This incident, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, underscores the political and theological gravity of the Qadariyyah movement during the early Caliphate, where denial of divine decree was seen as a challenge to both God's sovereignty and the Imam's authority. The severity of the punishment highlights the context of governance, where theological deviation was treated as a public threat to orthodoxy.
